seoTitle: Free Headline Analyzer for Blog and SEO Titles
metaDescription: Score headlines on length, numbers, power words and tone with a simple heuristic. Free, runs in your browser, and is not an SEO guarantee.
intro: Paste one or more headlines and get a score out of 100 based on length, numbers, power words, tone and structure, plus a note on whether the headline may truncate in search results.
why:
You often write ten possible titles for one article, and a decision based on gut feeling alone is shaky. A quick comparison on length, concrete numbers and strong words is a useful second opinion, especially when a title will be cut off in search results after around 60 characters.

This analyser applies a simple scoring recipe to each line: a sweet spot for length, a bonus for digits, a list of power words, a nudge for positive or negative tone, and a starter such as how or why. It prints the score, character count, word count and the power words found. The score is a heuristic and not a ranking or click-through prediction.
howTo: Paste your headlines, one per line.
Compare the scores, lengths and power words for each headline.
Shorten any headline flagged as possibly truncated, then rewrite and test again.

faq.a: It adds points for a length of about 40 to 65 characters, a number in the title, up to three power words, some emotional tone, a how or why opening and a moderate word count. It is a writing aid, not an SEO metric.

faq.q: Will a high score make my page rank?
faq.a: No. Rankings depend on content, links and many other factors. A better headline can help click-through, but the score has no connection to any search engine.

faq.q: Does it work for languages other than English?
faq.a: Not well. The power word and tone lists are English, so only length and numbers are meaningful in other languages.

faq.q: How can I check how the title looks in Google?
faq.a: Use the SERP Snippet or Title Length Checker. They show a preview and measure the title against typical display limits.
